sanskrit: madhye rājasahasrāṇāṃ prekṣakāṇāṃ samantataḥ kṛpayā ca punas tena jīveti sa visarjitaḥ
english: In the midst of thousands of kings looking on from every side, out of pity he was released by him with the words, "Live!"

sanskrit: tadavasthaḥ kṛtas tena somadatto 'tha māriṣa prasādayan mahādevam amarṣavaśam āsthitaḥ
english: Reduced to that condition by him, Somadatta then, O honored one, gave himself up to indignation and set about propitiating Mahādeva.

sanskrit: tasya tuṣṭo mahādevo varāṇāṃ varadaḥ prabhuḥ vareṇa chandayām āsa sa tu vavre varaṃ nṛpaḥ
english: Pleased with him, Mahādeva, the Lord, granter of boons among boons, offered him a choice; and that king chose his boon.

sanskrit: putram icchāmi bhagavan yo nihanyāc chineḥ sutam madhye rājasahasrāṇāṃ padā hanyāc ca saṃyuge
english: "I desire a son, O Blessed One, who shall slay the son of Śini, and in the midst of thousands of kings shall strike him down with his foot in battle."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā somadattasya pārthiva evam astv iti tatroktvā sa devo 'ntaradhīyata
english: Hearing those words of Somadatta, O king, the god said, "So be it," and there vanished.

sanskrit: sa tena varadānena labdhavān bhūridakṣiṇam nyapātayac ca samare saumadattiḥ śineḥ sutam
english: By that granting of the boon he obtained Bhūriśravas of abundant sacrificial gifts; and in battle the son of Somadatta did indeed lay low the son of Śini.

sanskrit: etat te kathitaṃ rājan yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi na hi śakyā raṇe jetuṃ sātvatā manujarṣabha
english: This have I told you, O king, concerning that whereof you ask me; the Sātvatas cannot be conquered in battle, O bull among men.

sanskrit: labdhalakṣyāś ca saṃgrāme bahavaś citrayodhinaḥ devadānavagandharvān vijetāro hy avismitāḥ svavīryavijaye yuktā naite paraparigrahāḥ
english: Many among them are sure of their aim in combat and fight with wondrous skill; unbewildered, they are conquerors of gods, dānavas, and gandharvas; bent upon victory won by their own valor, they are not subject to any other's possession.

sanskrit: na tulyaṃ vṛṣṇibhir iha dṛśyate kiṃ cana prabho bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyac ca balena bharatarṣabha
english: Nothing equal to the Vṛṣṇis is seen here, O lord—nothing that has been, that is, or that shall be, in strength, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: na jñātim avamanyante vṛddhānāṃ śāsane ratāḥ na devāsuragandharvā na yakṣoragarākṣasāḥ jetāro vṛṣṇivīrāṇāṃ na punar mānuṣā raṇe
english: They never slight a kinsman, and delight in the rule of their elders; neither gods, asuras, nor gandharvas, neither yakṣas, serpents, nor rākṣasas can vanquish the Vṛṣṇi heroes in war—still less men.

sanskrit: brahmadravye gurudravye jñātidravye 'py ahiṃsakāḥ eteṣāṃ rakṣitāraś ca ye syuḥ kasyāṃ cid āpadi
english: Toward the wealth of brahmins, of teachers, and of kinsmen they do no harm; and they are protectors of these, should any one of them fall into distress.

sanskrit: arthavanto na cotsiktā brahmaṇyāḥ satyavādinaḥ samarthān nāvamanyante dīnān abhyuddharanti ca
english: Wealthy yet not arrogant, devoted to brahmins, speakers of truth, they do not slight the powerful, and they raise up the wretched.

sanskrit: nityaṃ devaparā dāntā dātāraś cāvikatthanāḥ tena vṛṣṇipravīrāṇāṃ cakraṃ na pratihanyate
english: Ever devoted to the gods, self-controlled, generous, and free from boasting—therefore the wheel of the Vṛṣṇi heroes' dominion is never broken.

sanskrit: api meruṃ vahet kaś cit tared vā makarālayam na tu vṛṣṇipravīrāṇāṃ sametyāntaṃ vrajen nṛpa
english: One might bear Mount Meru, or swim across the abode of sea-monsters, but he could not, having met the Vṛṣṇi heroes, come to their end, O king.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yatra te saṃśayo vibho kururāja naraśreṣṭha tava hy apanayo mahān
english: All this have I declared to you, wherein your doubt lay, O mighty one; O king of the Kurus, best of men, great indeed is your misconduct.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tadavasthe hate tasmin bhūriśravasi kaurave yathā bhūyo 'bhavad yuddhaṃ tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When that Kaurava Bhūriśravas had been slain in such a plight, tell me, Saṃjaya, how the battle raged on once more.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca bhūriśravasi saṃkrānte paralokāya bhārata vāsudevaṃ mahābāhur arjunaḥ samacūcudat
english: Saṃjaya said: When Bhūriśravas had passed on to the other world, O Bhārata, the mighty-armed Arjuna urged Vāsudeva onward.

sanskrit: codayāśvān bhṛśaṃ kṛṣṇa yato rājā jayadrathaḥ astam eti mahābāho tvaramāṇo divākaraḥ
english: "Drive the horses hard, Kṛṣṇa, to where King Jayadratha is; the maker of day hastens, O mighty-armed one, to its setting."

sanskrit: etad dhi puruṣavyāghra mahad abhyudyataṃ mayā kāryaṃ saṃrakṣyate caiṣa kurusenāmahārathaiḥ
english: "For this great deed I have undertaken, O tiger among men; and this man is being guarded by the great chariot-warriors of the Kuru host."

sanskrit: nāstam eti yathā sūryo yathā satyaṃ bhaved vacaḥ codayāśvāṃs tathā kṛṣṇa yathā hanyāṃ jayadratham
english: "So drive the horses, Kṛṣṇa, that the sun shall not set, that my word may prove true, that I may slay Jayadratha."

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛṣṇo mahābāhū rajatapratimān hayān hayajñaś codayām āsa jayadratharathaṃ prati
english: Then the mighty-armed Kṛṣṇa, knower of horses, urged the silver-hued steeds onward toward the chariot of Jayadratha.

sanskrit: taṃ prayāntam amogheṣum utpatadbhir ivāśugaiḥ tvaramāṇā mahārāja senāmukhyāḥ samāvrajan
english: As he sped on, his shafts never failing, with arrows that flew as if leaping upward, the chief warriors of the host hastened to close round him, O great king.

sanskrit: duryodhanaś ca karṇaś ca vṛṣaseno 'tha madrarāṭ aśvatthāmā kṛpaś caiva svayam eva ca saindhavaḥ
english: Duryodhana and Karṇa and Vṛṣasena, the king of the Madras, Aśvatthāman and Kṛpa, and the lord of the Sindhus himself.

sanskrit: samāsādya tu bībhatsuḥ saindhavaṃ pramukhe sthitam netrābhyāṃ krodhadīptābhyāṃ saṃpraikṣan nirdahann iva
english: Drawing near, Bībhatsu beheld the lord of the Sindhus stationed at the front, and gazed upon him with eyes blazing with wrath, as if to burn him up.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā rādheyaṃ tvarito 'bravīt arjunaṃ vīkṣya saṃyāntaṃ jayadratharathaṃ prati
english: Then King Duryodhana, seeing Arjuna advancing toward Jayadratha's chariot, swiftly said to the son of Rādhā:

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa vaikartana yuddhakālo; vidarśayasvātmabalaṃ mahātman yathā na vadhyeta raṇe 'rjunena; jayadrathaḥ karṇa tathā kuruṣva
english: "This, O Vaikartana, is the hour of battle; show forth your own strength, great soul. So act, Karṇa, that Jayadratha be not slain by Arjuna in the fight."

sanskrit: alpāvaśiṣṭaṃ divasaṃ nṛvīra; vighātayasvādya ripuṃ śaraughaiḥ dinakṣayaṃ prāpya narapravīra; dhruvaṃ hi naḥ karṇa jayo bhaviṣyati
english: "Little of the day remains, O hero among men; strike down the foe now with floods of arrows. Once the day's end is reached, O foremost of men, our victory, Karṇa, shall surely be assured."

sanskrit: saindhave rakṣyamāṇe tu sūryasyāstamayaṃ prati mithyāpratijñaḥ kaunteyaḥ pravekṣyati hutāśanam
english: "If the lord of the Sindhus be but guarded until the setting of the sun, the son of Kuntī, his vow proved false, shall enter the fire."

sanskrit: anarjunāyāṃ ca bhuvi muhūrtam api mānada jīvituṃ notsaheran vai bhrātaro 'sya sahānugāḥ
english: "And on an earth bereft of Arjuna, O giver of honor, his brothers with their followers would not bear to live even for a moment."

sanskrit: vinaṣṭaiḥ pāṇḍaveyaiś ca saśailavanakānanām vasuṃdharām imāṃ karṇa bhokṣyāmo hatakaṇṭakām
english: "And with the sons of Pāṇḍu destroyed, we shall enjoy this earth, Karṇa, with its mountains, woods, and forests, its thorns plucked out."

sanskrit: daivenopahataḥ pārtho viparītaś ca mānada kāryākāryam ajānan vai pratijñāṃ kṛtavān raṇe
english: "Smitten by fate and turned awry, O giver of honor, Pārtha, not knowing the doable from the undoable, made his vow in battle."

sanskrit: nūnam ātmavināśāya pāṇḍavena kirīṭinā pratijñeyaṃ kṛtā karṇa jayadrathavadhaṃ prati
english: "Surely it was for his own destruction that the diademed son of Pāṇḍu made this vow, Karṇa, touching the slaying of Jayadratha."

sanskrit: kathaṃ jīvati durdharṣe tvayi rādheya phalgunaḥ anastaṃgata āditye hanyāt saindhavakaṃ nṛpam
english: "How, while you live, O unassailable son of Rādhā, shall Phalguna slay the Saindhava king before the sun has set?"

sanskrit: rakṣitaṃ madrarājena kṛpeṇa ca mahātmanā jayadrathaṃ raṇamukhe kathaṃ hanyād dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: "Jayadratha, guarded at the battle's front by the king of the Madras and by the great-souled Kṛpa—how shall Dhanaṃjaya slay him?"

sanskrit: drauṇinā rakṣyamāṇaṃ ca mayā duḥśāsanena ca kathaṃ prāpsyati bībhatsuḥ saindhavaṃ kālacoditaḥ
english: "And how, urged on by fate, shall Bībhatsu reach the lord of the Sindhus, who is guarded by Droṇa's son, by me, and by Duḥśāsana?"

sanskrit: yudhyante bahavaḥ śūrā lambate ca divākaraḥ śaṅke jayadrathaṃ pārtho naiva prāpsyati mānada
english: "Many heroes are fighting, and the sun hangs low; I think, O giver of honor, that Pārtha shall not reach Jayadratha at all."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ karṇa mayā sārdhaṃ śūraiś cānyair mahārathaiḥ yudhyasva yatnam āsthāya paraṃ pārthena saṃyuge
english: "Therefore, Karṇa, do you, together with me and with the other heroic great car-warriors, putting forth supreme effort, fight against Pārtha in the combat."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rādheyas tava putreṇa māriṣa duryodhanam idaṃ vākyaṃ pratyuvāca kurūttamam
english: Thus addressed by your son, O honored one, the son of Rādhā spoke these words in answer to Duryodhana, the foremost of the Kurus:

sanskrit: dṛḍhalakṣyeṇa śūreṇa bhīmasenena dhanvinā bhṛśam udvejitaḥ saṃkhye śarajālair anekaśaḥ
english: "Sorely harassed in the fray, time and again, by the bowman Bhīmasena—that hero of unerring aim—with his nets of arrows,

sanskrit: sthātavyam iti tiṣṭhāmi raṇe saṃprati mānada naivāṅgam iṅgati kiṃ cin me saṃtaptasya raṇeṣubhiḥ
english: "yet, resolved that I must stand, I stand even now in the battle, O giver of honor; though scorched by the shafts of war, no limb of mine so much as stirs."

sanskrit: yotsyāmi tu tathā rājañ śaktyāhaṃ parayā raṇe yathā pāṇḍavamukhyo 'sau na haniṣyati saindhavam
english: "I shall fight, O king, in battle with all my utmost might, so that that chief of the Pāṇḍavas shall not slay the lord of the Sindhus."

sanskrit: na hi me yudhyamānasya sāyakāṃś cāsyataḥ śitān saindhavaṃ prāpsyate vīraḥ savyasācī dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: "For while I fight and loose my whetted shafts, the hero Savyasācin Dhanaṃjaya shall not reach the lord of the Sindhus."

sanskrit: yat tu śaktimatā kāryaṃ satataṃ hitakāriṇā tat kariṣyāmi kauravya jayo daive pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: "Whatever ought to be done by one of power, who ever works for your good, that I shall do, O Kaurava; but victory rests with fate."

sanskrit: adya yotsye 'rjunam ahaṃ pauruṣaṃ svaṃ vyapāśritaḥ tvadarthaṃ puruṣavyāghra jayo daive pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: "Today I shall fight Arjuna, relying on my own manhood, for your sake, O tiger among men; but victory rests with fate."

sanskrit: adya yuddhaṃ kuruśreṣṭha mama pārthasya cobhayoḥ paśyantu sarvabhūtāni dāruṇaṃ lomaharṣaṇam
english: "Today, O best of the Kurus, let all beings behold the dreadful, hair-raising battle of us two, of mine and Pārtha's."

sanskrit: karṇakauravayor evaṃ raṇe saṃbhāṣamāṇayoḥ arjuno niśitair bāṇair jaghāna tava vāhinīm
english: While Karṇa and the Kaurava thus conversed in the field, Arjuna with his whetted shafts smote your host.

sanskrit: ciccheda tīkṣṇāgramukhaiḥ śūrāṇām anivartinām bhujān parighasaṃkāśān hastihastopamān raṇe
english: With keen-pointed arrows he severed in battle the arms of the unflinching heroes—arms like iron bars, like the trunks of elephants.

sanskrit: śirāṃsi ca mahābāhuś ciccheda niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ hastihastān hayagrīvā rathākṣāṃś ca samantataḥ
english: And the mighty-armed one clove with whetted shafts their heads, the trunks of elephants, the necks of horses, and the axles of chariots on every side.

sanskrit: śoṇitāktān hayārohān gṛhītaprāsatomarān kṣuraiś ciccheda bībhatsur dvidhaikaikaṃ tridhaiva ca
english: With razor-edged shafts Bībhatsu cleft, each into two and into three, the blood-drenched horsemen who gripped their lances and pikes.

sanskrit: hayavāraṇamukhyāś ca prāpatanta sahasraśaḥ dhvajāś chatrāṇi cāpāni cāmarāṇi śirāṃsi ca
english: And the foremost of horses and elephants fell by thousands, with banners, parasols, bows, yak-tail fans, and heads.

sanskrit: kakṣam agnim ivoddhūtaḥ pradahaṃs tava vāhinīm acireṇa mahīṃ pārthaś cakāra rudhirottarām
english: Burning your host like a fire blazing up through dry brushwood, in but a little while Pārtha made the earth flooded over with blood.

sanskrit: hatabhūyiṣṭhayodhaṃ tat kṛtvā tava balaṃ balī āsasāda durādharṣaḥ saindhavaṃ satyavikramaḥ
english: Having made the greater part of your army's warriors slain, the mighty, unassailable hero of true valor bore down upon the lord of the Sindhus.

sanskrit: bībhatsur bhīmasenena sātvatena ca rakṣitaḥ sa babhau bharataśreṣṭha jvalann iva hutāśanaḥ
english: Bībhatsu, guarded by Bhīmasena and by the Sātvata, shone forth, O best of the Bharatas, like a blazing fire.

sanskrit: taṃ tathāvasthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā tvadīyā vīryasaṃmatāḥ nāmṛṣyanta maheṣvāsāḥ phalgunaṃ puruṣarṣabhāḥ
english: Beholding Phalguna so stationed, your great bowmen, esteemed for their valor, bulls among men, could not endure it.

sanskrit: duryodhanaś ca karṇaś ca vṛṣaseno 'tha madrarāṭ aśvatthāmā kṛpaś caiva svayam eva ca saindhavaḥ
english: Duryodhana and Karṇa and Vṛṣasena, the king of the Madras, Aśvatthāman and Kṛpa, and the lord of the Sindhus himself—

sanskrit: saṃrabdhāḥ saindhavasyārthe samāvṛṇvan kirīṭinam nṛtyantaṃ rathamārgeṣu dhanurjyātalanisvanaiḥ
english: these, enraged, for the Saindhava's sake hemmed in the diademed one, who danced along the chariot-paths to the twang of his bowstring and the slap of his palm-guard.

sanskrit: saṃgrāmakovidaṃ pārthaṃ sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ abhītāḥ paryavartanta vyāditāsyam ivāntakam
english: All skilled in war, fearless, they closed round Pārtha, the master of combat, as round Death with gaping jaws.

sanskrit: saindhavaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā jighāṃsanto 'rjunācyutau sūryāstamayam icchanto lohitāyati bhāskare
english: Keeping the lord of the Sindhus behind them, seeking to slay Arjuna and Acyuta, they longed for the sun's setting as the day-maker turned red.

sanskrit: te bhujair bhogibhogābhair dhanūṃṣy āyamya sāyakān mumucuḥ sūryaraśmyābhāñ śataśaḥ phalgunaṃ prati
english: With arms like the coils of serpents they drew their bows and loosed by hundreds at Phalguna shafts that gleamed like the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: tān astān asyamānāṃś ca kirīṭī yuddhadurmadaḥ dvidhā tridhāṣṭadhaikaikaṃ chittvā vivyādha tān raṇe
english: But the diademed one, frenzied in battle, cleaving each of those loosed and flying shafts into two, three, and eight, pierced his foes in turn in the fray.

sanskrit: siṃhalāṅgūlaketus tu darśayañ śaktim ātmanaḥ śāradvatīsuto rājann arjunaṃ pratyavārayat
english: Then the son of Śāradvatī, whose banner bore the lion's tail, showing forth his own might, O king, withstood Arjuna.

sanskrit: sa viddhvā daśabhiḥ pārthaṃ vāsudevaṃ ca saptabhiḥ atiṣṭhad rathamārgeṣu saindhavaṃ paripālayan
english: Having pierced Pārtha with ten shafts and Vāsudeva with seven, he held his ground upon the chariot-paths, guarding the lord of the Sindhus.

sanskrit: athainaṃ kauravaśreṣṭhāḥ sarva eva mahārathāḥ mahatā rathavaṃśena sarvataḥ paryavārayan
english: Then all the foremost of the Kuru great car-warriors hemmed him in on every side with a vast array of chariots.

sanskrit: visphārayantaś cāpāni visṛjantaś ca sāyakān saindhavaṃ paryarakṣanta śāsanāt tanayasya te
english: Twanging their bows and loosing their shafts, they guarded the lord of the Sindhus round about, by the command of your son.

sanskrit: tatra pārthasya śūrasya bāhvor balam adṛśyata iṣūṇām akṣayatvaṃ ca dhanuṣo gāṇḍivasya ca
english: There was seen the strength of the heroic Pārtha's arms, the inexhaustibility of his arrows, and the might of his bow Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: astrair astrāṇi saṃvārya drauṇeḥ śāradvatasya ca ekaikaṃ navabhir bāṇaiḥ sarvān eva samarpayat
english: Warding off with his weapons the weapons of Droṇa's son and of the son of Śaradvat, he assailed every one of them, each with nine shafts.

sanskrit: taṃ drauṇiḥ pañcaviṃśatyā vṛṣasenaś ca saptabhiḥ duryodhanaś ca viṃśatyā karṇaśalyau tribhis tribhiḥ
english: Him Droṇa's son struck with twenty-five shafts, and Vṛṣasena with seven, Duryodhana with twenty, and Karṇa and Śalya each with three.

sanskrit: ta enam abhigarjanto vidhyantaś ca punaḥ punaḥ vidhunvantaś ca cāpāni sarvataḥ paryavārayan
english: Roaring at him and piercing him again and again, and shaking their bows, they hemmed him in on every side.

sanskrit: śliṣṭaṃ tu sarvataś cakrū rathamaṇḍalam āśu te sūryāstamayam icchantas tvaramāṇā mahārathāḥ
english: Those great car-warriors, longing for the sun's setting, swiftly drew their ring of chariots close-locked on every side.

sanskrit: ta enam abhinardanto vidhunvānā dhanūṃṣi ca siṣicur mārgaṇair ghorair giriṃ meghā ivāmbubhiḥ
english: Bellowing at him and shaking their bows, they drenched him with dreadful shafts as the clouds drench a mountain with their waters.

sanskrit: te mahāstrāṇi divyāni tatra rājan vyadarśayan dhanaṃjayasya gātreṣu śūrāḥ parighabāhavaḥ
english: There, O king, those heroes with arms like iron bars displayed their mighty celestial weapons upon the limbs of Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: hatabhūyiṣṭhayodhaṃ tat kṛtvā tava balaṃ balī āsasāda durādharṣaḥ saindhavaṃ satyavikramaḥ
english: Having made the greater part of your army's warriors slain, the mighty, unassailable hero of true valor bore down upon the lord of the Sindhus.

sanskrit: taṃ karṇaḥ saṃyuge rājan pratyavārayad āśugaiḥ miṣato bhīmasenasya sātvatasya ca bhārata
english: Him Karṇa withstood in the combat, O king, with his swift arrows, before the very eyes of Bhīmasena and of the Sātvata, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: taṃ pārtho daśabhir bāṇaiḥ pratyavidhyad raṇājire sūtaputraṃ mahābāhuḥ sarvasainyasya paśyataḥ
english: Him in turn the mighty-armed Pārtha pierced with ten shafts on the field of battle—the son of the charioteer—while all the host looked on.

sanskrit: sātvataś ca tribhir bāṇaiḥ karṇaṃ vivyādha māriṣa bhīmasenas tribhiś caiva punaḥ pārthaś ca saptabhiḥ
english: And the Sātvata pierced Karṇa with three shafts, O honored one, and Bhīmasena with three, and Pārtha again with seven.

sanskrit: tān karṇaḥ prativivyādha ṣaṣṭyā ṣaṣṭyā mahārathaḥ tad yuddham abhavad rājan karṇasya bahubhiḥ saha
english: Karṇa, the great car-warrior, pierced them each in return with sixty shafts; and so, O king, there arose that battle of Karṇa against many.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma sūtaputrasya māriṣa yad ekaḥ samare kruddhas trīn rathān paryavārayat
english: There we beheld a marvel in the son of the charioteer, O honored one—that, wrathful and alone in the fray, he held three chariot-warriors at bay.

sanskrit: phalgunas tu mahābāhuḥ karṇaṃ vaikartanaṃ raṇe sāyakānāṃ śatenaiva sarvamarmasv atāḍayat
english: But the mighty-armed Phalguna struck Karṇa Vaikartana in the battle, with a full hundred shafts, upon all his vital parts.

sanskrit: rudhirokṣitasarvāṅgaḥ sūtaputraḥ pratāpavān śaraiḥ pañcāśatā vīraḥ phalgunaṃ pratyavidhyata tasya tal lāghavaṃ dṛṣṭvā nāmṛṣyata raṇe 'rjunaḥ
english: His every limb bathed in blood, the valorous son of the charioteer, that hero, pierced Phalguna in return with fifty shafts; and seeing his deftness, Arjuna could not endure it in the fight.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārtho dhanuś chittvā vivyādhainaṃ stanāntare sāyakair navabhir vīras tvaramāṇo dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Then Pārtha, severing his bow, pierced him between the breasts; the hero Dhanaṃjaya did so in haste, with nine shafts.
